tools.label: Typographic arrows:
n.dropwrong1: And what exactly is that supposed to do?
n.typo_done: Yes, yes, you already found that one. Stop rubbing it in.
h.none: No ideas right now. Odd: I usually have too many.
card.ch10.label: Chapter 10
card.ch10.title: Errata (Part One)
end.ch10.title: End of Chapter 10
end.ch10.body:
The bridge, the door and the Hero are safe: they are now official corrections. But the Proofreader has taken the Pencil.
To be continued in Chapter 11.
rule.e1: P. 7, "the bridge is 3 metres long": read {}.
page.p31.title: Errata
page.p31.intro: For... read... Approved corrections go into the final edition and are no longer errors.
page.p31.sheet: Fig. 31 — Errata sheet, ready to attach
page.p31.margin: if an error becomes a correction, the proofreader can't touch it
page.p32.title: Spare words
page.p32.intro: Words left over from printing the previous chapters. Keep for any corrections.
page.p32.margin: we know some of these words very well
n.i1: The Print Shop. The press is running. And that's the proof sheet of the final edition.
c.i1: Welcome. You're just in time for printing.
c.i2: Errors to remove: a bridge that's too long, a door opened without a key, a Hero with his head on backwards.
n.i2: Those "errors" are us! The bridge we lengthened, the door we opened, the Hero we assembled!
p.i1: there's a way. an approved error isn't an error any more. it's called errata. page 31.
n.i3: "For... read...". The lines are empty. The spare words are on page 32.
n.empty1: Ink, paper, noise. The Proofreader's paradise.
n.empty2: Nothing there. Focus on the press.
n.tool1: The arrows won't help here. The right words in the right place will.
n.typo_press: "Proofredaer". On his own print shop. Let's not tell him. Actually, let's.
n.typo_lever: "Do not tuoch". The lever is safe, the spelling isn't.
n.tray: The enclosures tray. Whatever goes in gets printed together with the final edition.
n.proof: The proof sheet: the bridge, the door, the Hero. Each with a red X on top.
n.cup_empty: The pencil pot is empty. The Proofreader took her away.
p.cup1: i'm here, in the pencil pot. he put me in detention.
c.t1: Printing will start shortly. The errors' days are numbered.
c.t2: An edition without errors is a perfect edition. I don't understand why nobody wants to read it.
n.press: The press. It prints whatever the Proofreader approves. And erases the rest.
n.fix_bridge: "The bridge is 3 metres long: read 8 METRES". On the proof sheet the X on the bridge has become a tick.
n.fix_door: "The door: read door OPEN". The door is safe. The hole in the wall, less so.
n.fix_hero: "The Hero's head: read head BACK TO FRONT". The Hero is officially assembled that way. Forever.
c.perfect: PERFECT? I approve of the word. But it makes no sense on that line.
n.never: "NEVER"? That erases the error and the thing together. That's not what we want.
n.ready1: Three approved corrections! The errata sheet is ready, on page 31.
p.ready: attach it to the edition. the enclosures tray is under the press.
c.x1: An errata sheet? Attached to the final edition?
c.x2: "Read 8 metres". "Read door open". "Read head back to front".
c.x3: Then... they're not errors. They're corrections. Approved. I can't remove them.
c.x4: Only one error remains to be corrected. The one who made all the others.
p.x1: hey! let go of me! this wasn't favour number three!
c.x5: She will be corrected. In due course. In the next edition.
n.x3: ...To be continued. Really: it says so.
h.errata.1: The proof sheet wants to remove the bridge, the door and the Hero. The errata are on page 31.
h.errata.2: Each line of the errata is waiting for a word. The spare words are on page 32.
h.errata.3: Put 8 METRES on the bridge line, OPEN on the door line and BACK TO FRONT on the head line.
h.deliver.1: The errata are ready, but they need attaching to the final edition.
h.deliver.2: Under the press there's the enclosures tray.
h.deliver.3: Drag the errata sheet (page 31) onto the ENCLOSURES tray.
